title: Silicon photonics packaging and fiber coupling
bottleneck: Getting light on and off a photonic chip demands sub-micron alignment between fibers and grating or edge couplers, with active alignment that is slow and expensive. Unlike electronic packaging, there are no mature high-volume standards for photonic assembly and wafer-level test, so packaging can dominate total chip cost. Thermal drift further misaligns couplings in the field.
why_it_blocks: Packaging cost and complexity keep silicon photonics confined to high-margin transceivers instead of spreading into compute interconnects and sensors. Until photonic packaging approaches electronic-packaging economics, optical I/O can't go mainstream.
current_state: Co-packaged optics programs and automated passive-alignment techniques are advancing, with pilot production lines demonstrating progress. Wafer-scale photonic testing and low-cost assembly remain immature relative to CMOS packaging. Passive alignment techniques promise lower cost, but they demand component tolerances that today's photonic fabs struggle to hold.
